sections.category: Unsloth Studio's June build turns the local fine-tuning UI into an MCP-wired agent workbench

bullets.body: Unsloth pushed a fresh Studio build this week that moves its local fine-tuning UI well beyond train-and-chat and into MCP-connected agent territory. The headline addition is built-in Model Context Protocol support: Studio now ships with Context7, Exa, and Hugging Face MCP servers enabled by default, lets a locally-served model such as Gemma 4 or Qwen3.6 call those tools autonomously inside a single chat thread, and exposes a flow to add any custom MCP server by URL with OAuth or token authentication and automatic tool discovery, per the [Unsloth Documentation - How to Use MCP Servers with Local LLMs](https://unsloth.ai/docs/basics/mcp). The same build adds Data Recipes, a graph-based dataset workflow editor powered by NVIDIA Nemo Data Designer that ingests PDFs and CSVs, lets the user wire seed-data and generation blocks, preview sample output, and run a full synthetic-dataset build that feeds straight into a Studio fine-tune, per the [Unsloth Documentation - Unsloth Data Recipes](https://unsloth.ai/docs/new/studio/data-recipe). Alongside the MCP, Projects, Canvas, and rebuilt chat-UI work, the release continues Unsloth's hardware-coverage push from the prior week's CUDA 13.3 Windows binaries and Apple Silicon llama.cpp re-enablement out to NVIDIA Blackwell and B300 on Linux, and folds in Gemma 4 12B with a 256K-token context window as a runnable-and-trainable target on consumer-class memory. The throughline is that the same tool used to QLoRA a small open model now doubles as a tool-using local agent client and a synthetic-data factory, narrowing the gap between fine-tuning and shipping an agent on hardware the developer already owns.

sections.category: Snowflake Summit's Builder Keynote ships Iceberg v3 to GA and frames Cortex Sense, Datastream, and Adaptive Compute as the agentic-data stack

bullets.body: Snowflake Summit 26's Builder Keynote took the Wednesday June 3 9:00 AM PT slot at Moscone, and the substance underneath the agent demos is four infrastructure bets that decide whether the agentic-enterprise pitch holds. The one artifact that actually reached general availability at the show is Iceberg v3 with Polaris bi-directional writes, which lets external engines such as Spark and Trino write directly into Snowflake-managed tables through open standards with governance applied and no data duplication or downtime migration, with Affirm and Samsung Ads named as early adopters. The other three remain in preview: Cortex Sense, a metadata-to-ontology layer that sits on top of the Horizon Context governance layer and auto-builds a shared skills-and-semantics surface agents consume (Snowflake claims 3.5x better performance than Claude Code paired with MCP, a number unproven in production); Snowflake Datastream, a fully managed Kafka-compatible streaming service that takes existing Kafka producers with zero code changes; and Adaptive Compute, which auto-sizes warehouses in real time to kill manual tuning, per the [Futurum - Snowflake Summit 2026: four infrastructure bets that determine whether the agentic enterprise delivers](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/snowflake-summit-2026-four-infrastructure-bets-that-determine-whether-the-agentic-enterprise-delivers/). The keynote anchored the story in live customer agents rather than slides: BlackRock demonstrated using Horizon Context so its agents operate on one shared definition of enterprise truth, and Sanofi showed an agent called Concierge that preps sales reps for physician visits off live data, the same week Sanofi named Snowflake as the backbone for its AI-powered drug-development work, per [BusinessWire - Sanofi Chooses Snowflake to Accelerate its AI-Powered Drug Development](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260602582503/en/Sanofi-Chooses-Snowflake-to-Accelerate-its-AI-Powered-Drug-Development).

sections.category: Broadcom's Q2 report puts custom-AI-accelerator revenue at $10.8B and guides Q3 AI to roughly $16B

bullets.body: Broadcom reported fiscal Q2 2026 results after the close on June 3, and the AI-silicon line is the whole story. Consolidated revenue hit a record $22.2 billion, up 48% year over year, but the standout is AI semiconductor revenue of $10.8 billion, up 143%, driven by custom AI accelerators (Broadcom's XPUs) and AI networking, per [Grafa - Broadcom reports Q2 earnings: AI chip revenue jumps 143%](https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/broadcom-q2-fy26-earnings-ai-growth). On the call, CEO Hock Tan guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue to approximately $16 billion, over 200% year-over-year growth, and disclosed that bookings for AI semiconductors topped $30 billion in the quarter against the $10.8 billion shipped, while reiterating Broadcom's position supplying XPUs and the components that enable them to its six core custom-silicon customers; total Q3 revenue is guided to about $29.4 billion, up 84%. Infrastructure software, the VMware-anchored segment, added $7.2 billion, up 9%, with Q3 guided near $8.9 billion. Free cash flow set a record at $10.3 billion and non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.44, and the stock rose about 2.6% in after-hours trading to roughly $494, per the [Investing.com - Broadcom Q2 2026 earnings beat, stock rises (earnings-call transcript)](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-broadcom-q2-2026-earnings-beat-stock-rises-93CH-4674808). The read-through is that the custom-ASIC alternative to merchant GPUs is now compounding faster than the GPU incumbent's own growth rate, with a backlog that pre-commits multiples of current shipments.

sections.category: Bay Area June-July events: Snowflake Summit and Microsoft Build close today, then WWDC, Databricks, and the AI Engineer World's Fair

bullets.body: Today is the back half of the dense San Francisco conference window. Snowflake Summit 26 runs Monday-Thursday June 1-4 at Moscone Center, with the Builder Keynote of live agent demos happening this morning (Wednesday June 3, 9:00 AM PT) and the show floor open through Thursday, per [Moscone Center - Snowflake Summit 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/snowflake-summit-2026). Microsoft Build 2026 reaches its final day today at Fort Mason Center (Tuesday-Wednesday June 2-3), with the Wednesday program centered on live GitHub, Copilot, and Visual Studio agent sessions. AI Tinkerers SF still has an Advanced MCP Showcase sponsored by WorkOS and a Voice Agents Science Fair sponsored by ElevenLabs on its June calendar, per the [AI Tinkerers SF - events](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/) hub. Apple WWDC26 runs Monday-Friday June 8-12 at Apple Park, with the keynote and Platforms State of the Union on Monday June 8 (keynote 10:00 AM PT), per [Apple Developer - WWDC26](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/). Databricks Data + AI Summit runs Monday-Thursday June 15-18 across Moscone with 800+ sessions spanning data engineering, governance, analytics, applications, and agents, per [Moscone Center - Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/databricks-data-ai-summit-2026). The AI Engineer World's Fair runs at Moscone West with New Engineer Orientation and badge pickup on Sunday June 28 (Day 0) and the main program Monday June 29 through Thursday July 2 — 29 tracks, 300+ speakers, and 6,000+ AI engineers, founders, and VPs of AI, per the [AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026) site. Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas (re:Inforce merged in) with registration opening June 16.
